prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1398; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck pain and headache at the scene and was transported to a local emergency department for evaluation. Preliminary liability appears to favor the claimant, pending statements from both drivers and review of any available dashcam footage.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports being diagnosed with a concussion and advised to limit screen time and rest. Claimant states they are not represented by an attorney and has not yet consulted one. Explained the claims process, the available coverage under the policy, and the claimant's right to seek independent advice. Requested copies of all medical records and discharge paperwork.

Entry 3: Obtained a recorded statement from the insured driver. Insured states they checked the mirror and signaled but did not see the claimant's vehicle in the adjacent lane. Insured acknowledges contact occurred as they merged. Requested the insured's photos of both vehicles and the scene. Vehicle inspection scheduled for the claimant's vehicle at the preferred repair facility.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's emergency department records, which document a diagnosis of concussion with no fracture on imaging. Claimant reports ongoing headaches and difficulty concentrating at work. Reviewed the file with the supervisor. Claimant's treating physician has recommended follow-up in two weeks. Reserves adjusted to reflect the medical component. Sent the claimant a written summary of their rights and a list of documents still needed.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with the claimant. Claimant is still experiencing headaches but reports slight improvement. Confirmed the rental vehicle arrangement and the repair estimate timeline. Provided the claimant with the adjuster contact information and advised that additional medical documentation from the follow-up visit would help move the bodily injury evaluation forward. Diary set for review once the follow-up records are received.
